newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais repel refugees fleeing Khmer Rouge fighting.
newsitem.headline: Thais repel refugees fleeing Khmer Rouge fighting.

text.p: Thai soldiers on Friday pushed back more than 200 refugees who had fled into Thailand to escape fighting among rival Khmer Rouge guerrilla factions in northern Cambodia, army sources said.

The refugees were supporters of dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary. They fled after fighters from the group's hardline faction, led by Pol Pot, attacked their village on Wednesday in Joop Kaki in northeastern Oddar Meanchey province.
"We are now trucking them back," said an army source in northeastern Laharnsai town on the Thai side of the border.
A total of 230 refugees, mostly women and children, were being returned, the source told Reuters.
The refugees would be taken to safer areas of Cambodia opposite Thailand's Thapraya district, the sources said. The area is about 100 km (62 miles) south of their village.
Joop Kaki, previously controlled by Ieng Sary's dissident faction, was the first village to be captured by the hardliners.

Ieng Sary, former foreign minister of the Khmer Rouge when they ruled Cambodia in the mid-1970s, left the main group last month. The Khmer Rouge's clandestine radio has called for the destruction of Ieng Sary and military commanders loyal to him.
Ieng Sary has sought peace with the Cambodian government. Cambodian defence minister Tea Banh has pledged to send troops to help him fight his former hardline comrades.
